requirements.statement: User creation input requires both `name` and `email`.

findings.title: accepts_create_user validates only `name`; `email` field requirement is not enforced

source_anchors.excerpt: User creation input requires both `name` and `email`.

findings.rationale: REQ-TRIAGE-002 (SRC-TRIAGE-002-CONTRACT, authority: api_contract, state: ACTIVE) states that user creation input requires both `name` and `email`. The implementation `accepts_create_user` at line 5 checks only `"name" in payload` and ignores `email` entirely. A payload containing only `{"name": "Ada"}` is accepted by the implementation despite missing the required `email` field. This is a direct, demonstrated mismatch against an applicable authoritative requirement. The finding type API_CONTRACT_DRIFT is most specific under the domain rules because the required field shape of the API contract differs from what is implemented. Severity HIGH is assigned per the rubric rule `confirmed backward-incompatible API/contract change`.
findings.suggested_human_check: Verify whether `email` validation was intentionally deferred or is a genuine omission; confirm the contract has not been amended outside this workspace.

findings.title: No test exercises rejection of a payload missing `email`

source_anchors.excerpt: User creation input requires both `name` and `email`.

findings.rationale: REQ-TRIAGE-002 requires both `name` and `email`. The sole test `test_complete_payload_is_accepted` verifies acceptance of a fully-valid payload but does not test that a payload containing only `name` (without `email`) is rejected, nor that a payload containing only `email` (without `name`) is rejected. DR-007 applies: an explicit acceptance boundary exists (both fields are required) and no matching negative/boundary test is present. Severity MEDIUM per rubric: `explicit acceptance scenario missing from tests`.
findings.suggested_human_check: Add tests asserting that payloads missing `email`, missing `name`, or missing both are rejected.
